t: Lesson 6, Commands. Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
This is how you stop typing the same prompt every day.
If you keep pasting the same prompt, it's time for a command.
Type a slash in a word, and the whole prompt runs.
Add a word after it to point it at what matters today.
Here's a review command. Front matter at the top describes it.
A slot catches whatever you type after the command.
And the body is just the prompt.
Each harness calls them something slightly different.
Commands, prompts, or workflows. Same idea, different folder.
Keep them in Get. Write one file per command.
Commit it next to the code. And the whole team gets it on their next pull.
Quick recap. A command is a saved prompt with front matter, arguments, and a body.
Your mission, turn the prompt you paste most often into a slash command and commit it.
Your best prompts are now one keystroke away.
